chapter: Chicago: Henderson, Tatum and Roy Eldridge, then New York and the army
title: Carter's Kelly's Stables bill; the draft notice and Carter's appeal
summary: The Kelly's show with Carter, Nat Cole's trio, Tatum and Miss Rhapsody; later at the Apollo Collins was drafted and Carter appeared with him before the board.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So I stayed in New York and went to work with Benny. And let's see now, who was on this bill? I think it was Benny Carter, and Nat, and his trio, Art Tatum, and we had a singer by the name of Miss Rhapsody. She didn't call herself Miss Raspody-- Rhapsody, it was Miss Raspody, you know. And I think this whole show cost him around $900.00 a week, you know. This was just the --

Let's see, Benny had four rhythm and three horn. A baritone saxophone, a trumpet and Benny played alto and trumpet, or whatever. You know, whatever he felt like playing. He played everything, you know. But a beautiful experience. And after we left there Benny formed a bigger band and I worked with him then, and we went to the Apollo Theatre, and this is where I got my greetings from Uncle Sam. And Benny -- I was so upset, and so Benny said, well John, look, I'm going to go before the board with you. And Benny went before the board with me to try to get me out of the army and they almost got Benny. We laugh about this now, but I left Benny Carter's band to go into the army.
